enforcer.xptrigger: You addressed a challenge with violence or intimidation.

id-00001.name: Battleborn
id-00001.text: You may expend your special armor to reduce harm from an attack in combat or to push yourself during a fight.
id-00001.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you "reduce harm" that means the level of harm you're facing right now is reduced by one. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00002.name: Bodyguard
id-00002.text: When you protect a teammate, take +1d to your resistance roll. When you gather info to anticipate possible threats in the current situation, you get +1 effect.
id-00002.note: The protect teamwork maneuver lets you face a consequence for a teammate. If you choose to resist that consequence, this ability gives you +1d to your resistance roll. Also, when you read a situation to gather information about hidden dangers or potential attackers, you get +1 effect—which means more detailed information.

id-00003.name: Arcane fighter
id-00003.text: You may imbue your hands, melee weapons, or tools with spirit energy. You gain potency in combat vs. the supernatural..
id-00003.note: When you imbue yourself with arcane energy, how do you do it? What does it look like when the energy manifests?

id-00004.name: Leader
id-00004.text: When you Command a cohort in combat, they continue to fight when they would otherwise break (they're not taken out when they suffer level 3 harm). They gain +1 effect and 1 armor.
id-00004.note: This ability makes your cohorts more effective in battle and also allows them to resist harm by using armor. While you lead your cohorts, they won't stop fighting until they take fatal harm (level 4) or you order them to cease. What do you do to inspire such bravery in battle?

id-00005.name: Mule
id-00005.text: Your load limits are higher. Light: 5. Normal: 7. Heavy: 8.
id-00005.note: This ability is great if you want to wear heavy armor and pack a heavy weapon without attracting lots of attention. Since your exact gear is determined on-the-fly during an operation, having more load also gives you more options to get creative with when dealing with problems during a score.

id-00006.name: Not to be trifled with
id-00006.text: You can push yourself to do one of the following: perform a feat of physical force that verges on the superhuman—engage a small gang on equal footing in close combat.
id-00006.note: When you push yourself to activate this ability, you still get one of the normal benefits of pushing yourself (+1d, +1 effect, etc.) in addition to the special ability. If you perform a feat that verges on the superhuman, you might break a metal weapon with your bare hands, tackle a galloping horse, lift a huge weight, etc. If you engage a small gang on equal footing, you don't suffer reduced effect due to scale against a small gang (up to six people).

id-00007.name: Savage
id-00007.text: When you unleash physical violence, it's especially frightening. When you Command a frightened target, take +1d.
id-00007.note: You instill fear in those around you when you get violent. How they react depends on the person. Some people will flee from you, some will be impressed, some will get violent in return. The GM judges the response of a given NPC. In addition, when you Command someone who's affected by fear (from this ability or otherwise), take +1d to your roll.

id-00008.name: Vigorous
id-00008.text: You recover from harm faster. Permanently fill in one of your healing clock segments. Take +1d to healing treatment rolls.
id-00008.note: Your healing clock becomes a 3-clock, and you get a bonus die when you recover.

id-00001.name: Sharpshooter
id-00001.text: You can push yourself to do one of the following: make a ranged attack at extreme distance beyond what's normal for the weapon—unleash a barrage of rapid fire to suppress the enemy.
id-00001.note: When you push yourself to activate this ability, you still get one of the normal benefits of pushing yourself (+1d, +1 effect, etc.) in addition to the special ability. The first use of this ability allows you to attempt long-range sniper shots that would otherwise be impossible with typical rudimentary firearms. The second use allows you to keep up a steady rate of fire in a battle (enough to "suppress" a small gang up to six people), rather than stopping for a slow reload or discarding a gun after each shot. When an enemy is suppressed, they're reluctant to maneuver or attack (usually calling for a fortune roll to see if they can manage it).

id-00002.name: Focused
id-00002.text: You may expend your special armor to resist a consequence of surprise or mental harm (fear, confusion, losing track of someone) or to push yourself for ranged combat or tracking.
id-00002.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you "resist a consequence" of the appropriate type, you avoid it completely. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00003.name: Scout
id-00003.text: When you gather information to discover the location of a target, you get +1 effect. When you hide in a prepared position or use camouflage you get +1d to rolls to avoid detection.
id-00003.note: A "target" can be a person, a destination, a good ambush spot, an item, etc.

id-00004.name: Tough as nails
id-00004.text: Penalties from harm are one level less severe (though level 4 harm is still fatal).
id-00004.note: With this ability, level 3 harm doesn't incapacitate you; instead you take -1d to your rolls (as if it were level 2 harm). Level 2 harm affects you as if it were level 1 (less effect). Level 1 harm has no effect on you (but you still write it on your sheet, and must recover to heal it). Record the harm at its original level—for healing purposes, the original harm level applies.

id-00005.name: Vengeful
id-00005.text: You gain an additional xp trigger: You got payback against someone who harmed you or someone you care about. If your crew helped you get payback, also mark crew xp.

tinker.xptrigger: You addressed a challenge with technical skill or mayhem.

id-00001.name: Alchemist
id-00001.text: When you invent or craft a creation with alchemical features, you get +1 result level to your roll (a 1-3 becomes a 4/5, etc.). You begin with one special formula already known.
id-00001.note: Follow the Inventing procedure with the GM to define your first special alchemical formula.

id-00002.name: Analyst
id-00002.text: During downtime, you get two ticks to distribute among any long term project clocks that involve investigation or learning a new formula or design plan.

id-00003.name: Artificer
id-00003.text: When you invent or craft a creation with spark-craft features, you get +1 result level to your roll (a 1-3 becomes a 4/5, etc.). You begin with one special design already known.
id-00003.note: Follow the Inventing procedure with the GM to define your first spark-craft design.

id-00004.name: Fortitude
id-00004.text: You may expend your special armor to resist a consequence of fatigue, weakness, or chemical effects, or to push yourself when working with technical skill or handling alchemicals.
id-00004.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you "resist a consequence" of the appropriate type, you avoid it completely. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00005.name: Supernatural ward
id-00005.text: When you Wreck an area with arcane substances, ruining it for any other use, it becomes anathema or enticing to the supernatural (your choice).
id-00005.note: If you make an area anathema to the supernatural, they will do everything they can to avoid it, and will suffer torment if forced inside the area. If you make an area enticing to spirits, they will seek it out and linger in the area, and will suffer torment if forced to leave. This effect lasts for several days over an area the size of a small room. Particularly powerful or prepared entities may roll their quality or arcane magnitude to see how well they're able to resist the effect.

id-00006.name: Saboteur
id-00006.text: When you Wreck, your work is much quieter than it should be and the damage is very well-hidden from casual inspection.
id-00006.note: You can drill holes in things, melt stuff with acid, even use a muffled explosive, and it will all be very quiet and extremely hard to notice.

burglar.name: Burglar
burglar.xptrigger: You addressed a challenge with stealth or evasion.

id-00001.name: Infiltrator
id-00001.text: You are not affected by quality or Tier when you bypass security measures.
id-00001.note: This ability lets you contend with higher-Tier enemies on equal footing. When you're cracking a safe, picking a lock, or sneaking past elite guards, your effect level is never reduced due to superior Tier or quality level of your opposition. Are you a renowned safe cracker? Do people tell stories of how you slipped under the noses of two Chief Inspectors, or are your exceptional talents yet to be discovered?

id-00002.name: Ambush
id-00002.text: When you attack from hiding or spring a trap, you get +1d to your roll.
id-00002.note: This ability benefits from preparation— so don't forget you can do that in a flashback.

id-00003.name: Daredevil
id-00003.text: When you roll a desperate action, you get +1d to your roll if you also take -1d to any resistance rolls against consequences from your action.
id-00003.note: This special ability is a bit of a gamble. The bonus die helps you, but if you suffer consequences, they'll probably be more costly to resist. But hey, you're a daredevil, so no big deal, right?

id-00004.name: The devil's footsteps
id-00004.text: You can push yourself to do one of the following: perform a feat of athletics that verges on the superhuman—maneuver to confuse your enemies so they mistakenly attack each other.
id-00004.note: When you push yourself to activate this ability, you still get one of the normal benefits of pushing yourself (+1d, +1 effect, etc.) if you're making a roll, in addition to the special ability. If you perform an athletic feat (running, tumbling, balance, climbing, etc.) that verges on the superhuman, you might climb a sheer surface that lacks good hand-holds, tumble safely out of a three-story fall, leap a shocking distance, etc. If you maneuver to confuse your enemies, they attack each other for a moment before they realize their mistake. The GM might make a fortune roll to see how badly they harm or interfere with each other.

id-00005.name: Expertise
id-00005.text: Choose one of your action ratings. When you lead a group action using that action, you can suffer only 1 stress at most, regardless of the number of failed rolls.
id-00005.note: This special ability is good for covering for your team. If they're all terrible at your favored action, you don't have to worry about suffering a lot of stress when you lead their group action.

id-00006.name: Reflexes
id-00006.text: When there's a question about who acts first, the answer is you.
id-00006.note: This ability gives you the initiative in most situations. Some specially trained NPCs might also have reflexes, but otherwise, you're always the first to act, and can interrupt anyone else who tries to beat you to the punch. This ability usually doesn't negate the need to make an action roll that you would otherwise have to make, but it may improve your position or effect.

id-00007.name: Shadow
id-00007.text: You may expend your special armor to resist a consequence from detection or security measures, or to push yourself for a feat of athletics or stealth.
id-00007.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you "resist a consequence" of the appropriate type, you avoid it completely. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00001.name: Rook's gambit
id-00001.text: Take 2 stress to roll your best action rating while performing a different action. Say how you adapt your skill to this use.
id-00001.note: This is the "jack-of-all-trades" ability. If you want to attempt lots of different sorts of actions and still have a good dice pool to roll, this is the special ability for you.

id-00002.name: Like looking into a mirror
id-00002.text: You can always tell when someone is lying to you.
id-00002.note: This ability works in all situations without restriction. It is very powerful, but also a bit of a curse. You see though every lie, even the kind ones.

id-00003.name: A little something on the side
id-00003.text: At the end of each downtime phase, you earn +2 stash.
id-00003.note: Since this money comes at the end of downtime, after all downtime actions are resolved, you can't remove it from your stash and spend it on extra activities until your next downtime phase.

id-00004.name: Mesmerism
id-00004.text: When you Sway someone, you may cause them to forget that it's happened until they next interact with you.
id-00004.note: The victim's memory "glosses over" the missing time, so it's not suspicious that they've forgotten something. When you next interact with the victim, they remember everything clearly, including the strange effect of this ability.

id-00005.name: Subterfuge
id-00005.text: You may expend your special armor to resist a consequence from suspicion or persuasion, or to push yourself for subterfuge.
id-00005.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you "resist a consequence" of the appropriate type, you avoid it completely. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00006.name: Trust in me
id-00006.text: You get +1d vs. a target with whom you have an intimate relationship.
id-00006.note: This ability isn't just for social interactions. Any action can get the bonus. "Intimate" is for you and the group to define, it need not exclusively mean romantic intimacy.

schemer.xptrigger: You addressed a challenge with calculation or conspiracy.

id-00001.name: Foresight
id-00001.text: Two times per score you can assist a teammate without paying stress. Describe how you prepared for this.
id-00001.note: You can narrate an event in the past that helps your teammate now, or you might explain how you expected this situation and planned a helpful contingency that you reveal now.

id-00002.name: Calculating
id-00002.text: Due to your careful planning, during downtime, you may give yourself or another crew member +1 downtime activity.
id-00002.note: If you forget to use this ability during downtime, you can still activate it during the score and flashback to the previous downtime when the extra activity happened.

id-00003.name: Connected
id-00003.text: During downtime, you get +1 result level when you acquire an asset or reduce heat.
id-00003.note: Your array of underworld connections can be leveraged to loan assets, pressure a vendor to give you a better deal, intimidate witnesses, etc.

id-00004.name: Mastermind
id-00004.text: You may expend your special armor to protect a teammate, or to push yourself when you gather information or work on a long-term project.
id-00004.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you protect a teammate, this ability negates or reduces the severity of a consequence or harm that your teammate is facing. You don't have to be present to use this ability—say how you prepared for this situation in the past. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00005.name: Weaving the web
id-00005.text: You gain +1d to Consort when you gather information on a target for a score. You get +1d to the engagement roll for that operation.
id-00005.note: Your network of underworld connections can always be leveraged to gain insight for a job—even when your contacts aren't aware that they're helping you.

occultist.xptrigger: You addressed a challenge with knowledge or arcane power.

id-00001.name: Arcane mind
id-00001.text: You're always aware of supernatural entities in your presence. Take +1d whenever you gather information about the supernatural by any means.

id-00002.name: Iron will
id-00002.text: You are immune to the terror that some supernatural entities inflict on sight. When you make a resistance roll with Resolve, take +1d.
id-00002.note: With this ability, you do not freeze up or flee when confronted by any kind of supernatural entity or strange occult event.

id-00003.name: Ritual
id-00003.text: You know the arcane methods to perform ritual sorcery. You can Study an occult ritual (or create a new one) to summon a supernatural effect or being. You begin with one ritual already learned.
id-00003.note: Without this special ability, the study and practice of rituals leaves you utterly vulnerable to the powers you supplicate. Such endeavors are not recommended.

id-00001.name: Canal-born
id-00001.text: Your family has lived on Brackwater's canals for generations: barge folk, lock-keepers, net-menders.

id-00002.name: Marshland
id-00002.text: From the reed villages of the salt marshes beyond the sea wall, where the old ways are still kept.

id-00003.name: Highlands
id-00003.text: Hill and mine country to the north: hard winters, hard people, long memories.

id-00004.name: Far Isles
id-00004.text: The scattered islands across the grey sea, whose ships still bring spice, silk and refugees.

id-00005.name: Eastern Provinces
id-00005.text: The heart of the old empire, far inland: an accent the city's nobles both envy and mock.

id-00006.name: Mixed
id-00006.text: A family from more than one place, at home in none of them. Write the two lands.

id-00001.name: Scholar

id-00002.name: Labor
id-00002.text: Docker, factory hand, barge-puller, servant, miner: work that breaks the body.

id-00003.name: Law
id-00003.text: Watch constable, bailiff, clerk of the courts, informant, prison guard.

id-00004.name: Trade
id-00004.text: Shopkeeper, merchant's runner, artisan, peddler, moneylender.

id-00005.name: Military
id-00005.text: Soldier, marine, quartermaster, deserter or veteran of some war abroad.

id-00006.name: Gentry
id-00006.text: Minor nobility or old money fallen on hard times, or the servant who knew their secrets.

id-00007.name: Underworld
id-00007.text: Born to it: pickpocket, lookout, runner for a gang, a fence's errand child.

id-00001.name: Faith
id-00001.text: You're dedicated to an unseen power, forgotten god, ancestor, etc.

id-00002.name: Gambling
id-00002.text: You crave games of chance, betting on sporting events, etc.

id-00003.name: Luxury
id-00003.text: Expensive or ostentatious displays of opulence.

id-00004.name: Obligation
id-00004.text: You're devoted to a family, a cause, an organization, a charity, etc.

id-00005.name: Pleasure
id-00005.text: Gratification from lovers, food, drink, drugs, art, theater, etc.

id-00006.name: Stupor
id-00006.text: You seek oblivion in the abuse of drugs, drinking to excess, getting beaten to a pulp in the fighting pits, etc.

id-00007.name: Weird
id-00007.text: You experiment with strange essences, consort with rogue spirits, observe bizarre rituals or taboos, etc.

id-00001.name: Cold
id-00001.text: You're not moved by emotional appeals or social bonds.

id-00002.name: Haunted
id-00002.text: You're often lost in reverie, reliving past horrors, seeing things.

id-00003.name: Obsessed
id-00003.text: You're enthralled by one thing: an activity, a person, an ideology.

id-00004.name: Paranoid
id-00004.text: You imagine danger everywhere; you can't trust others.

id-00005.name: Reckless
id-00005.text: You have little regard for your own safety or best interests.

id-00006.name: Soft
id-00006.text: You lose your edge; you become sentimental, passive, gentle.

id-00007.name: Unstable
id-00007.text: Your emotional state is volatile. You can instantly rage, or fall into despair, act impulsively, or freeze up.

id-00008.name: Vicious
id-00008.text: You seek out opportunities to hurt people, even for no good reason.

id-00001.text: Select or roll an additional entanglement.

id-00002.name: Brag
id-00002.text: You brag about your exploits: the crew takes +2 heat.

id-00003.name: Lost
id-00003.text: Your character vanishes for a few weeks: play a different character until this one returns (healed of any harm).

id-00004.name: Tapped
id-00004.text: Your current purveyor cuts you off: find a new source for your vice.

id-00001.name: Boat house
id-00001.text: You have a boat, a dock on a waterway, and a small shack to store boating supplies. A second upgrade improves the boat with armor and more cargo capacity.

id-00002.name: Carriage House

id-00003.name: Hidden Lair
id-00003.text: Your lair has a secret location and is disguised to hide it from view. If your lair is discovered, use two downtime activities and pay coin equal to your Tier to relocate it and hide it once again.

id-00004.name: Quarters
id-00004.text: Your lair includes living quarters for the crew. Without this upgrade, each PC sleeps elsewhere, and is vulnerable when they do so.

id-00005.name: Secure Lair
id-00005.text: Your lair has locks, alarms, and traps to thwart intruders. A second upgrade improves the defenses to include arcane measures that work against spirits. You might roll your crew's Tier if these measures are ever put to the test, to see how well they thwart an intruder.

id-00006.name: Vault
id-00006.text: Your lair has a secure vault, increasing your storage capacity for coin to 8. A second upgrade increases your capacity to 16. A separate part of your vault can be used as a holding cell.

id-00007.name: Workshop
id-00007.text: Your lair has a workshop appointed with tools for tinkering and alchemy, as well as a small library of books, documents, and maps. You may accomplish long-term projects with these assets without leaving your lair.

id-00001.name: Battleborn
id-00001.text: You may expend your special armor to reduce harm from an attack in combat or to push yourself during a fight.
id-00001.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you "reduce harm" that means the level of harm you're facing right now is reduced by one. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00002.name: Bodyguard
id-00002.text: When you protect a teammate, take +1d to your resistance roll. When you gather info to anticipate possible threats in the current situation, you get +1 effect.
id-00002.note: The protect teamwork maneuver lets you face a consequence for a teammate. If you choose to resist that consequence, this ability gives you +1d to your resistance roll. Also, when you read a situation to gather information about hidden dangers or potential attackers, you get +1 effect—which means more detailed information.

id-00003.name: Arcane fighter
id-00003.text: You may imbue your hands, melee weapons, or tools with spirit energy. You gain potency in combat vs. the supernatural..
id-00003.note: When you imbue yourself with arcane energy, how do you do it? What does it look like when the energy manifests?

id-00004.name: Leader
id-00004.text: When you Command a cohort in combat, they continue to fight when they would otherwise break (they're not taken out when they suffer level 3 harm). They gain +1 effect and 1 armor.
id-00004.note: This ability makes your cohorts more effective in battle and also allows them to resist harm by using armor. While you lead your cohorts, they won't stop fighting until they take fatal harm (level 4) or you order them to cease. What do you do to inspire such bravery in battle?

id-00005.name: Mule
id-00005.text: Your load limits are higher. Light: 5. Normal: 7. Heavy: 8.
id-00005.note: This ability is great if you want to wear heavy armor and pack a heavy weapon without attracting lots of attention. Since your exact gear is determined on-the-fly during an operation, having more load also gives you more options to get creative with when dealing with problems during a score.

id-00006.name: Not to be trifled with
id-00006.text: You can push yourself to do one of the following: perform a feat of physical force that verges on the superhuman—engage a small gang on equal footing in close combat.
id-00006.note: When you push yourself to activate this ability, you still get one of the normal benefits of pushing yourself (+1d, +1 effect, etc.) in addition to the special ability. If you perform a feat that verges on the superhuman, you might break a metal weapon with your bare hands, tackle a galloping horse, lift a huge weight, etc. If you engage a small gang on equal footing, you don't suffer reduced effect due to scale against a small gang (up to six people).

id-00007.name: Savage
id-00007.text: When you unleash physical violence, it's especially frightening. When you Command a frightened target, take +1d.
id-00007.note: You instill fear in those around you when you get violent. How they react depends on the person. Some people will flee from you, some will be impressed, some will get violent in return. The GM judges the response of a given NPC. In addition, when you Command someone who's affected by fear (from this ability or otherwise), take +1d to your roll.

id-00008.name: Vigorous
id-00008.text: You recover from harm faster. Permanently fill in one of your healing clock segments. Take +1d to healing treatment rolls.
id-00008.note: Your healing clock becomes a 3-clock, and you get a bonus die when you recover.

id-00009.name: Sharpshooter
id-00009.text: You can push yourself to do one of the following: make a ranged attack at extreme distance beyond what's normal for the weapon—unleash a barrage of rapid fire to suppress the enemy.
id-00009.note: When you push yourself to activate this ability, you still get one of the normal benefits of pushing yourself (+1d, +1 effect, etc.) in addition to the special ability. The first use of this ability allows you to attempt long-range sniper shots that would otherwise be impossible with typical rudimentary firearms. The second use allows you to keep up a steady rate of fire in a battle (enough to "suppress" a small gang up to six people), rather than stopping for a slow reload or discarding a gun after each shot. When an enemy is suppressed, they're reluctant to maneuver or attack (usually calling for a fortune roll to see if they can manage it).

id-00010.name: Focused
id-00010.text: You may expend your special armor to resist a consequence of surprise or mental harm (fear, confusion, losing track of someone) or to push yourself for ranged combat or tracking.
id-00010.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you "resist a consequence" of the appropriate type, you avoid it completely. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00011.name: Scout
id-00011.text: When you gather information to discover the location of a target, you get +1 effect. When you hide in a prepared position or use camouflage you get +1d to rolls to avoid detection.
id-00011.note: A "target" can be a person, a destination, a good ambush spot, an item, etc.

id-00012.name: Tough as nails
id-00012.text: Penalties from harm are one level less severe (though level 4 harm is still fatal).
id-00012.note: With this ability, level 3 harm doesn't incapacitate you; instead you take -1d to your rolls (as if it were level 2 harm). Level 2 harm affects you as if it were level 1 (less effect). Level 1 harm has no effect on you (but you still write it on your sheet, and must recover to heal it). Record the harm at its original level—for healing purposes, the original harm level applies.

id-00013.name: Vengeful
id-00013.text: You gain an additional xp trigger: You got payback against someone who harmed you or someone you care about. If your crew helped you get payback, also mark crew xp.

id-00014.name: Alchemist
id-00014.text: When you invent or craft a creation with alchemical features, you get +1 result level to your roll (a 1-3 becomes a 4/5, etc.). You begin with one special formula already known.
id-00014.note: Follow the Inventing procedure with the GM to define your first special alchemical formula.

id-00015.name: Analyst
id-00015.text: During downtime, you get two ticks to distribute among any long term project clocks that involve investigation or learning a new formula or design plan.

id-00016.name: Artificer
id-00016.text: When you invent or craft a creation with spark-craft features, you get +1 result level to your roll (a 1-3 becomes a 4/5, etc.). You begin with one special design already known.
id-00016.note: Follow the Inventing procedure with the GM to define your first spark-craft design.

id-00017.name: Fortitude
id-00017.text: You may expend your special armor to resist a consequence of fatigue, weakness, or chemical effects, or to push yourself when working with technical skill or handling alchemicals.
id-00017.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you "resist a consequence" of the appropriate type, you avoid it completely. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00018.name: Supernatural ward
id-00018.text: When you Wreck an area with arcane substances, ruining it for any other use, it becomes anathema or enticing to the supernatural (your choice).
id-00018.note: If you make an area anathema to the supernatural, they will do everything they can to avoid it, and will suffer torment if forced inside the area. If you make an area enticing to spirits, they will seek it out and linger in the area, and will suffer torment if forced to leave. This effect lasts for several days over an area the size of a small room. Particularly powerful or prepared entities may roll their quality or arcane magnitude to see how well they're able to resist the effect.

id-00019.name: Saboteur
id-00019.text: When you Wreck, your work is much quieter than it should be and the damage is very well-hidden from casual inspection.
id-00019.note: You can drill holes in things, melt stuff with acid, even use a muffled explosive, and it will all be very quiet and extremely hard to notice.

id-00020.name: Infiltrator
id-00020.text: You are not affected by quality or Tier when you bypass security measures.
id-00020.note: This ability lets you contend with higher-Tier enemies on equal footing. When you're cracking a safe, picking a lock, or sneaking past elite guards, your effect level is never reduced due to superior Tier or quality level of your opposition. Are you a renowned safe cracker? Do people tell stories of how you slipped under the noses of two Chief Inspectors, or are your exceptional talents yet to be discovered?

id-00021.name: Ambush
id-00021.text: When you attack from hiding or spring a trap, you get +1d to your roll.
id-00021.note: This ability benefits from preparation— so don't forget you can do that in a flashback.

id-00022.name: Daredevil
id-00022.text: When you roll a desperate action, you get +1d to your roll if you also take -1d to any resistance rolls against consequences from your action.
id-00022.note: This special ability is a bit of a gamble. The bonus die helps you, but if you suffer consequences, they'll probably be more costly to resist. But hey, you're a daredevil, so no big deal, right?

id-00023.name: The devil's footsteps
id-00023.text: You can push yourself to do one of the following: perform a feat of athletics that verges on the superhuman—maneuver to confuse your enemies so they mistakenly attack each other.
id-00023.note: When you push yourself to activate this ability, you still get one of the normal benefits of pushing yourself (+1d, +1 effect, etc.) if you're making a roll, in addition to the special ability. If you perform an athletic feat (running, tumbling, balance, climbing, etc.) that verges on the superhuman, you might climb a sheer surface that lacks good hand-holds, tumble safely out of a three-story fall, leap a shocking distance, etc. If you maneuver to confuse your enemies, they attack each other for a moment before they realize their mistake. The GM might make a fortune roll to see how badly they harm or interfere with each other.

id-00024.name: Expertise
id-00024.text: Choose one of your action ratings. When you lead a group action using that action, you can suffer only 1 stress at most, regardless of the number of failed rolls.
id-00024.note: This special ability is good for covering for your team. If they're all terrible at your favored action, you don't have to worry about suffering a lot of stress when you lead their group action.

id-00025.name: Reflexes
id-00025.text: When there's a question about who acts first, the answer is you.
id-00025.note: This ability gives you the initiative in most situations. Some specially trained NPCs might also have reflexes, but otherwise, you're always the first to act, and can interrupt anyone else who tries to beat you to the punch. This ability usually doesn't negate the need to make an action roll that you would otherwise have to make, but it may improve your position or effect.

id-00026.name: Shadow
id-00026.text: You may expend your special armor to resist a consequence from detection or security measures, or to push yourself for a feat of athletics or stealth.
id-00026.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you "resist a consequence" of the appropriate type, you avoid it completely. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00027.name: Rook's gambit
id-00027.text: Take 2 stress to roll your best action rating while performing a different action. Say how you adapt your skill to this use.
id-00027.note: This is the "jack-of-all-trades" ability. If you want to attempt lots of different sorts of actions and still have a good dice pool to roll, this is the special ability for you.

id-00028.name: Like looking into a mirror
id-00028.text: You can always tell when someone is lying to you.
id-00028.note: This ability works in all situations without restriction. It is very powerful, but also a bit of a curse. You see though every lie, even the kind ones.

id-00029.name: A little something on the side
id-00029.text: At the end of each downtime phase, you earn +2 stash.
id-00029.note: Since this money comes at the end of downtime, after all downtime actions are resolved, you can't remove it from your stash and spend it on extra activities until your next downtime phase.

id-00030.name: Mesmerism
id-00030.text: When you Sway someone, you may cause them to forget that it's happened until they next interact with you.
id-00030.note: The victim's memory "glosses over" the missing time, so it's not suspicious that they've forgotten something. When you next interact with the victim, they remember everything clearly, including the strange effect of this ability.

id-00031.name: Subterfuge
id-00031.text: You may expend your special armor to resist a consequence from suspicion or persuasion, or to push yourself for subterfuge.
id-00031.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you "resist a consequence" of the appropriate type, you avoid it completely. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00032.name: Trust in me
id-00032.text: You get +1d vs. a target with whom you have an intimate relationship.
id-00032.note: This ability isn't just for social interactions. Any action can get the bonus. "Intimate" is for you and the group to define, it need not exclusively mean romantic intimacy.

id-00033.name: Foresight
id-00033.text: Two times per score you can assist a teammate without paying stress. Describe how you prepared for this.
id-00033.note: You can narrate an event in the past that helps your teammate now, or you might explain how you expected this situation and planned a helpful contingency that you reveal now.

id-00034.name: Calculating
id-00034.text: Due to your careful planning, during downtime, you may give yourself or another crew member +1 downtime activity.
id-00034.note: If you forget to use this ability during downtime, you can still activate it during the score and flashback to the previous downtime when the extra activity happened.

id-00035.name: Connected
id-00035.text: During downtime, you get +1 result level when you acquire an asset or reduce heat.
id-00035.note: Your array of underworld connections can be leveraged to loan assets, pressure a vendor to give you a better deal, intimidate witnesses, etc.

id-00036.name: Mastermind
id-00036.text: You may expend your special armor to protect a teammate, or to push yourself when you gather information or work on a long-term project.
id-00036.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you protect a teammate, this ability negates or reduces the severity of a consequence or harm that your teammate is facing. You don't have to be present to use this ability—say how you prepared for this situation in the past. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00037.name: Weaving the web
id-00037.text: You gain +1d to Consort when you gather information on a target for a score. You get +1d to the engagement roll for that operation.
id-00037.note: Your network of underworld connections can always be leveraged to gain insight for a job—even when your contacts aren't aware that they're helping you.

id-00038.name: Arcane mind
id-00038.text: You're always aware of supernatural entities in your presence. Take +1d whenever you gather information about the supernatural by any means.

id-00039.name: Iron will
id-00039.text: You are immune to the terror that some supernatural entities inflict on sight. When you make a resistance roll with Resolve, take +1d.
id-00039.note: With this ability, you do not freeze up or flee when confronted by any kind of supernatural entity or strange occult event.

id-00040.name: Ritual
id-00040.text: You know the arcane methods to perform ritual sorcery. You can Study an occult ritual (or create a new one) to summon a supernatural effect or being. You begin with one ritual already learned.
id-00040.note: Without this special ability, the study and practice of rituals leaves you utterly vulnerable to the powers you supplicate. Such endeavors are not recommended.

id-00041.name: Strange methods
id-00041.text: When you invent or craft a creation with arcane features, get +1 result level to your roll (a 1-3 becomes a 4/5, etc.). You begin with one arcane design already known.
id-00041.note: Follow the Inventing procedure with the GM to define your first arcane design.

id-00042.name: Warded
id-00042.text: You may expend your special armor to resist a supernatural consequence, or to push yourself when you contend with or employ arcane forces.
id-00042.note: When you use this ability, tick the special armor box on your playbook sheet. If you resist a consequence, this ability negates or reduces its severity. If you use this ability to push yourself, you get one of the benefits (+1d, +1 effect, act despite severe harm) but you don't take 2 stress. Your special armor is restored at the beginning of downtime.

id-00001.name: Deadly
id-00001.text: Each PC may add +1 action rating to Hunt, Prowl, or Skirmish (up to a max rating of 3).
id-00001.note: Each player may choose the action they prefer (you don't all have to choose the same one). If you take this ability during initial character and crew creation, it supersedes the normal starting limit for action ratings.

id-00002.name: Death veil
id-00002.text: Due to hard-won experience or occult ritual, you don't take extra heat when killing is involved on a score.

id-00003.name: No traces
id-00003.text: When you keep an operation quiet or make it look like an accident, you get half the rep value of the target (round up) instead of zero. When you end downtime with zero heat, take +1 rep.
id-00003.note: There are many clients who value quiet operations. This ability rewards you for keeping a low-profile.

id-00004.name: Patron
id-00004.text: When you advance your Tier, it costs half the coin it normally would.
id-00004.note: Who is your patron? Why do they help you?

id-00005.name: Predators
id-00005.text: When you use a stealth or deception plan to commit murder, take +1d to the engagement roll.
id-00005.note: This ability applies when the goal is murder. It doesn't apply to other stealth or deception operations you attempt that happen to involve killing.

id-00006.name: Fiends
id-00006.text: Fear is as good as respect. You may count each wanted level as if it were turf.
id-00006.note: The maximum wanted level is 4. Regardless of how much turf you hold (from this ability or otherwise) the minimum rep cost to advance your Tier is always 6.

id-00007.name: Forged in the fire
id-00007.text: Each PC has been toughened by cruel experience. You get +1d to resistance rolls.
id-00007.note: This ability applies to PCs in the crew. It doesn't confer any special toughness to your cohorts.

id-00008.name: War dogs
id-00008.text: When you're at war (-3 faction status), your crew does not suffer -1 hold and PCs still get two downtime activities, instead of just one.

id-00009.name: Anointed
id-00009.text: You gain +1d to resistance rolls against supernatural threats. You get +1d to healing rolls when you have supernatural harm.

id-00010.name: Accord
id-00010.text: Sometimes friends are as good as territory. You may treat up to three +3 faction statuses you hold as if they are turf.
id-00010.note: If your status changes, you lose the turf until it becomes +3 again. Regardless of how much turf you hold (from this ability or otherwise) the minimum rep cost to advance your Tier is always 6.

id-00011.name: High society
id-00011.text: It's all about who you know. Take -1 heat during downtime and +1d to gather information about the city's elite.

id-00012.name: Pack rats
id-00012.text: Your lair is a jumble of stolen items. When you roll to acquire an asset, take +1d.
id-00012.note: This ability might mean that you actually have the item you need in your pile of stuff, or it could mean you have extra odds and ends to barter with.

id-00013.name: Second story
id-00013.text: When you execute a clandestine infiltration, you get +1d to the engagement roll.

id-00014.name: Synchronized
id-00014.text: When you perform a group action, you may count multiple 6s from different rolls as a critical success.
id-00014.note: For example, Lyric leads a group action to Attune to the ghost field to overcome a magical ward on the Dimmer Sisters' door. Emily, Lyric's player, rolls and gets a 6, and so does Matt! Because the crew has Synchronized, their two separate 6s count as a critical success on the roll.

id-00015.name: All hands
id-00015.text: During downtime, one of your cohorts may perform a downtime activity for the crew to acquire an asset, reduce heat, or work on a long-term project.

id-00016.name: Just passing through
id-00016.text: During downtime, take -1 heat. When your heat is 4 or less, you get +1d to deceive people when you pass yourselves off as ordinary citizens.
